name: seo-traffic-airlock
title: SEO Traffic Airlock
description:
A quiet way to lose all your search traffic: a staging robots.txt with "Disallow: /" gets deployed, or a site migration ships a redirect loop. Nothing errors, and the damage shows up days later. This module is the check to run before the change goes live, whether an AI agent or a person is making it. It is read-only and fully offline: it deploys nothing, fetches nothing, and has zero network access.

WHO IT IS FOR
Small teams and agencies that let an agent or a script touch robots.txt, redirects or site migrations, and want a signed record that the change was checked first.

COMMANDS (2)
seo.audit_robots_txt - paste a candidate robots.txt and optional test paths. It is evaluated with the matching rules crawlers use (RFC 9309: wildcards, $, longest match wins, one most-specific group per crawler) and returns a verdict of OK, REVIEW or BLOCKS_SITE. It catches the phrasings naive checks miss, such as "Disallow: / # temporary", a lowercase "googlebot" group, "Disallow: /*", and rules placed before any User-agent line.
seo.preview_redirect_graph - paste proposed rules ("/old -> /new", one per line or separated by ;). It finds loops, rules that feed a loop, self-redirects, conflicting duplicate sources, chains (with the direct target to use instead) and oversized batches. Malformed rules are refused, never skipped.

EXAMPLE
audit_robots_txt with "User-agent: *" and "Disallow: / # temporary", testing /, /products: BLOCKS_SITE, a critical SITE_WIDE_BLOCK finding, and both paths shown as disallowed by the rule "Disallow: /".
preview_redirect_graph with "/old -> /new; /new -> /final; /a -> /b; /b -> /a": UNSAFE. It reports the loop /a -> /b -> /a, and that /old takes 2 hops and should point straight at /final.

TRUST
No network, no credentials, no filesystem writes, no subprocess. The sandbox declares this, and both commands were tested with network sockets disabled. Every run returns a signed receipt. 59 unit tests, standard library only.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
It reports; it does not block or deploy anything, so it only protects you if it runs before the change (for example as a gate in a workflow). It checks the robots.txt text you give it and does not fetch your live file. Paths are compared as written (no percent-decoding) and redirect rules as exact strings. If a form field strips line breaks, paste into a multi-line field or type \n between lines; a flattened file is refused rather than guessed.
